scope: Time-boxed search (about 45 minutes, 14:40-15:20) for an Earth-supported law of whole snow-aggregate breakup in collisions and under drag or turbulence.
finding: No usable law found; the load analogy (turbulence_survival.md) remains, with its limits stated in breakup_literature.md.
external_bytes: No papers or datasets added to the repository; one retrieved PDF hash recorded.

sources.authors: Takeshi Sato, Kenji Kosugi, Shigeto Mochizuki and Masaki Nemoto
sources.title: Fracture and accumulation conditions of snowflakes on the snow surface
sources.publication: Proceedings of the International Snow Science Workshop 2006, Telluride, Colorado, pp. 203-210
sources.obtained: Full PDF fetched 25 October 2026 and read through pdftotext; the PDF was not retained in the repository.
sources.reading_extent: Abstract, methods, analysis and results sections 1-4.2, Tables 1-2, Figs. 3-7 captions and text.
sources.evidence: Cold wind-tunnel experiment (-7 C) with artificial aggregates of dendrites (sieve sizes 7 and 20 mm) falling onto soft (about 150 kg/m3) and hard snow surfaces; field video of natural flakes up to about 10 mm at -0.1 to -1.4 C, Shinjo, February 2004.

quantities.horizontal_impact: Vih = 0.8 Uset; U1 = 0.8 Uset for the fracture parameterization, so Vih equals U1
quantities.compressive_fracture: Observed at the normal impact and deliberately not scored by the authors

sources.use: Impact speed at which loose dendritic aggregates fail in shear against a rigid surface; compared with closing speeds from differential settling aloft.
sources.limit: Surface impacts, not collisions between falling aggregates; one temperature in the laboratory; fracture judged by eye in five levels.

sources.title: Fragmentation of ice particles: laboratory experiments on graupel-graupel and graupel-snowflake collisions
sources.obtained: Publisher article page fetched 25 October 2026 (abstract and results text as rendered); corrigendum already recorded in strength_sources.json on 21 October.

quantities.fragments_per_collision: about 50 to more than 400; 70-500 in the abstract
quantities.central_collisions: snowflake completely broken; edge collisions rotate it with partial breakage

sources.use: Lowest measured energy at which a dense impactor destroys a centimetre flake; fragment sizes.
sources.limit: Dense graupel impactor; artificial dendrites grown near 120% ice saturation; the 2024 corrigendum reduced the fitted asperity density fourfold, and whether the page values include it was not checked.
sources.reading_extent: Article page as rendered: abstract, results text and fitted parameters; figures not inspected.

sources.title: Fragmentation in Collisions of Snow with Graupel/Hail: New Formulation from Field Observations
sources.obtained: Search-engine summary of the abstract, 25 October 2026; the publisher page refused access (HTTP 403). Fuller reading recorded in strength_sources.json on 21 October.
sources.use: Fragment numbers from natural snow on ice spheres.
sources.limit: Chipping counts from snow on dense ice; no whole-aggregate failure.
sources.reading_extent: Abstract only (publisher page HTTP 403 on 25 October); fuller passages read on 21 October are recorded in strength_sources.json.

sources.title: Improved Formulation of Fragmentation of Snow during Collision with Graupel/Hail based on Observations at Jungfraujoch: Cold Non-Dendritic Regime of Temperature
sources.obtained: Title and search-engine summary only, 25 October 2026.
sources.use: Confirms the fragmentation literature continues to address snow on graupel/hail.

sources.authors: Vaughan T. J. Phillips, Jun-Ichi Yano and Alexander Khain
sources.title: Ice Multiplication by Breakup in Ice-Ice Collisions. Part I: Theoretical Formulation
sources.obtained: Search-engine summary of the formulation, 25 October 2026; the form matches the implementation in aggregation.py (20 October).
sources.use: Fragment counts from branch chipping; tested on 20 October in aggregation.py, where it changed lunar flake sizes by 10-25% without capping them.
sources.limit: Chips small fragments; no whole-aggregate failure.
sources.reading_extent: Formulation only, from search summaries and the 20 October implementation; the publisher page was not read (AMS pages refused access).

sources.authors: K. Kenneth Lo and Richard E. Passarelli Jr.
sources.title: The Growth of Snow in Winter Storms: An Airborne Observational Study
sources.obtained: Abstract through search-engine summaries and the CrossRef record, 25 October 2026; the publisher page refused access (HTTP 403).

sources.limit: No rate law, strength or limiting-slope values obtained.
